title: Iran Pushes for BRICS Bank Membership as Araghchi Calls Modi Talks 'Strong'
excerpt: On the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, Iran's foreign minister said Tehran is “working on” New Development Bank membership, with some countries already supportive.
body:
• Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Saturday in New Delhi that Tehran is "working on" membership in the BRICS New Development Bank, with some countries already supportive and requirements being fulfilled.
  • Araghchi described Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian's bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi as a "strong meeting," in an interview with Iran's SNN on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit.
  • He highlighted Friday's BRICS commercial council discussions, where Putin, Modi, and Pezeshkian discussed settling trade in local and national currencies — a conversation that "caught the attention of the world."
  • Iran's NDB bid was first announced last month by Central Bank of Iran Governor Abdolnaser Hemmati; membership would give Tehran a new economic lifeline as U.S. sanctions pressure intensifies.

Iran has stepped up its bid to join the BRICS New Development Bank, with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi saying on Saturday that Tehran has secured support from some countries and is now working to complete the requirements for membership. Araghchi, who is in New Delhi for the 18th BRICS Summit, also described Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian's meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi as a "strong" one, while highlighting Iran's expanding engagement with BRICS members.

Speaking to Iranian outlet SNN Iran on Saturday, Araghchi framed the summit's main session — which begins today — as the centerpiece of a packed diplomatic program. "Yesterday, a commercial council was formed, and you were a witness to important discussions that took place. Mr Putin, Mr Modi, and Dr Pezeshkian, especially regarding the use of local currencies and national currencies, had a conversation that caught the attention of the world and attracted a lot of news coverage," he said.

The NDB bid

When asked about Iran's bid to join the New Development Bank, the minister said: "We are working on that today, and some countries are supportive, and they are in the process of fulfilling the necessary requirements." Iran's intent to join the NDB was first announced last month by Central Bank of Iran Governor Abdolnaser Hemmati, according to TV BRICS, which cited Iranian media.

The New Development Bank, headquartered in Shanghai, was created by BRICS to fund infrastructure and sustainable development in emerging economies as an alternative to Western-dominated lending institutions. For Iran, membership would open a financing channel independent of the dollar-based system — a strategic prize as Washington ramps up sanctions pressure and warns of consequences for Tehran's trading partners.

A packed bilateral schedule

Araghchi detailed Pezeshkian's diplomatic calendar around the summit. The bilateral with Modi took place on Friday; Saturday brings the main summit session alongside meetings with Malaysia and Ethiopia, the latter described by Araghchi as an important African country. "Bilateral issues are being raised, regional issues are being raised, and the Islamic Republic of Iran's relations are expanding with the collection of Islamic countries and the countries of the region, and this is evident in all the meetings," he said.

"Mr Putin, Mr Modi, and Dr Pezeshkian, especially regarding the use of local currencies and national currencies, had a conversation that caught the attention of the world and attracted a lot of news coverage."

— Abbas Araghchi, Iranian Foreign Minister, in an interview with SNN Iran

The Modi-Pezeshkian meeting came less than two weeks after the two leaders reaffirmed their "longstanding" strategic partnership. Pezeshkian had urged Modi to use India's extensive contacts with various parties to help move away from war and bloodshed toward dialogue and agreement, according to the official handout. The high-level discussions took place against the backdrop of ongoing conflicts in West Asia affecting regional stability, commercial navigation, and maritime logistics — with Chabahar Port, the strategic project giving India a trade route bypassing Pakistan, remaining a priority, alongside energy linkages.

An economic lifeline play

Tehran's NDB push is inseparable from its economic predicament. With the U.S. imposing fresh sanctions pressure and explicitly warning Iran's trading partners, the Islamic Republic is working to deepen ties with Moscow and Beijing while cultivating alternatives. The New Delhi summit gives Tehran a rare chance to engage several of its largest remaining economic partners — China, India, Russia, and the UAE — collectively, in a single room, six months after war broke out between the U.S. and Iran.

What's next

NDB membership requires approval from the bank's existing shareholders, so Tehran's lobbying will continue on the summit's sidelines and beyond. Watch whether the summit's final declaration references new NDB membership applications, whether the local-currency trade discussion produces concrete settlement mechanisms, and how the Modi-Pezeshkian commitments on Chabahar and energy cooperation translate into agreements. The 18th BRICS Summit runs September 12–13 in New Delhi.
nri_angle: A deeper India-Iran economic partnership, via Chabahar and local-currency trade, matters to Indian businesses and diaspora professionals engaged in Gulf and West Asia commerce.
author: Diaspora Desk
